doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: His father's discipline about the left hand and playing every note better
summary: His father told him to play even one whole note better each night and insisted on a strict left hand.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: about the fact that the singers, you know you’re playing the same thing over and over again. He said, “Anytime that you’re able to have your instrument in your hand is a moment of reverie.” And he said, “If your responsibility tonight is to do nothing but play one whole note C, play it better tonight than you played it last night, with the resolve that you’ll play it better tomorrow than you play it tonight.” And he used to make me — he would allow no slack in my left hand. When my hands would hurt, my fingers would be sore, and the muscles in here just feel like they’re going to pop, he told me that the sound was coming from my left hand, and he was very strict about my left hand being correct at all times. Never relaxing. So when you talk about my sound, that’s something that has been my predominant goal.
